definition: Sex reassignment, in this packet, refers to sex reassignment surgery used as part of care for people with gender dysphoria. It is presented alongside cross-sex hormone treatment as a medical option intended to improve quality of life.

reasons: The packet mentions sex reassignment surgery (SRS) mainly in terms of its discontinuation/resumption, but it does not support the definition’s claim that SRS is “used as part of care” for people with gender dysphoria.
The packet supports quality-of-life improvement for cross-sex hormone treatment (CSHT), but it does not state that sex reassignment surgery (SRS) is intended to improve quality of life.

The packet discusses CSHT and psychotherapy, and mentions SRS only indirectly; the definition presents SRS and CSHT together as a medical option to improve quality of life, which is not fully supported by the supplied text.
The packet supports sex reassignment surgery and cross-sex hormone treatment as distinct items, but it does not define the term "sex reassignment" as specifically meaning surgery.

The statement that sex reassignment is "presented alongside cross-sex hormone treatment as a medical option intended to improve quality of life" goes beyond the packet; only cross-sex hormone treatment is explicitly described as an option to improve quality of life.
The definition adds a clinical framing about "care for people with gender dysphoria" that is only partly supported and is broader and more specific than the packet warrants.
